title: A minimal prime on a Noetherian affine chart gives a stalk annihilator
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $U\subseteq T$ be an affine open, and let $y\in U$. Put $A=\mathcal O_T(U)$ and identify $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Suppose $A$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and the prime $\mathfrak p_y\subset A$ corresponding to $y$ is minimal, meaning that no prime of $A$ is strictly contained in $\mathfrak p_y$. Then there exists $w\in\mathcal O_{T,y}$ with $\operatorname{Ann}_{\mathcal O_{T,y}}(w)=\mathfrak m_y$, where $\operatorname{Ann}_{\mathcal O_{T,y}}(w)=\{r\in\mathcal O_{T,y}:rw=0\}$ and $\mathfrak m_y$ is the maximal ideal of the local ring $\mathcal O_{T,y}$. In particular $y\in\operatorname{Ass}_T(\mathcal O_T)$ [def-sc-associated-points].

source.place: Tag 02OK (lemma-associated-affine-open), forward implication for the structure sheaf, with Algebra Tag 05BV (lemma-ass-minimal-prime-support) applied to the ring as a module over itself.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-minimal-prime-associated] to the commutative ring $A$ and the prime $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak p_y$. The hypotheses that $A$ is Noetherian and that $\mathfrak p$ contains no smaller prime are exactly those of the item. Choose $z\in A$ with $\operatorname{Ann}_A(z)=\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Tag 05BV (lemma-ass-minimal-prime-support), specialized to the ring as a module over itself.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization](c), applied to $T,U,y$, the germ map induces a ring isomorphism $\theta:A_{\mathfrak p}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal O_{T,y}$. By [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $A_{\mathfrak p}$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak p A_{\mathfrak p}$. A ring isomorphism preserves units in both directions, hence identifies the ideals of nonunits of these local rings. Consequently $\theta(\mathfrak p A_{\mathfrak p})=\mathfrak m_y$.

source.place: Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves), part (6), with the open-subspace stalk identification (Example 01HF, example-open-subspace).

proof.text: Compute the annihilator of $z/1$ directly using the fractions of [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. If $(a/s)(z/1)=0$, then $taz=0$ for some $t\notin\mathfrak p$. Thus $ta\in\operatorname{Ann}_A(z)=\mathfrak p$, and primality gives $a\in\mathfrak p$, so $a/s\in\mathfrak p A_{\mathfrak p}$. Conversely, each $b\in\mathfrak p$ kills $z$; its image $b/1$ therefore kills $z/1$, and every element of the ideal generated by these images also kills $z/1$. This proves $\operatorname{Ann}_{A_{\mathfrak p}}(z/1)=\mathfrak p A_{\mathfrak p}$.

source.place: Tag 0310 (lemma-associated-primes-localize), proof of (1); the annihilator calculation is written out from the zero-fraction criterion.

proof.text: Set $w=\theta(z/1)$. For $r\in\mathcal O_{T,y}$, write $r=\theta(q)$ using surjectivity. Then $rw=\theta(q(z/1))=0$ if and only if $q(z/1)=0$, by injectivity. Steps 2 and 3 give $\operatorname{Ann}_{\mathcal O_{T,y}}(w)=\theta(\mathfrak p A_{\mathfrak p})=\mathfrak m_y$. This is an associated-prime witness for the stalk module over itself; hence $y\in\operatorname{Ass}_T(\mathcal O_T)$ by [def-sc-associated-points].

proof_origin.place: Tag 02OK (lemma-associated-affine-open), proof of (1), with Algebra Tag 05BV supplying the initial annihilator and the Tag 0310 zero-fraction calculation made explicit.
